verdict.rationale: mParticle documents its own environment flag: every Events API batch can be marked "development" instead of "production" (SDKs set it via isDevelopmentMode), which keeps test data apart from production data. That is data segregation within the same account, not an isolated sandbox. The evidence says there is no separate sandbox instance or test tenant and that the word sandbox never appears in the API docs, so isolation is only logical. missing for 10: a dedicated sandbox or test workspace isolated from the production account, documentation of how dev-mode data is kept from production audiences and outputs, and independent or hands-on corroboration.

support.subject: As an AI-native user, I can test against a sandbox environment without touching production data

citations.quote: which segregates development data from production data within the same account
This is a per-event environment flag, not a separate sandbox instance or test tenant
